summary: OpenAI's model that matches images with text descriptions, so you can classify images using plain-language labels.

heroCommands.command:
pip install ftfy regex tqdm
pip install git+https://github.com/openai/CLIP.git

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training) is a neural network trained on many image and text pairs. Given an image, it can predict the most relevant text snippet in natural language, without being trained directly for that task, similar to zero-shot abilities in GPT models.
sixtySeconds.problem: Classic image classifiers only know fixed labels. CLIP lets you describe your own labels in words and score an image against them.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for the original, widely used image-text model with a simple Python API and MIT license.

overview: Install PyTorch and torchvision, then the small dependencies (ftfy, regex, tqdm) and the repo as a Python package from GitHub. Use cpuonly instead of a CUDA toolkit on machines without a GPU.
Load a model such as ViT-B/32 with clip.load, preprocess an image, tokenize candidate texts, then compute image and text features and the label probabilities.
CLIP is MIT licensed; see the model card for limitations.
limitations: Original install targets older PyTorch versions
Has known biases described in the model card

firstRun.title: Score an image against labels
firstRun.code:
import torch
import clip
from PIL import Image

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
model, preprocess = clip.load("ViT-B/32", device=device)

image = preprocess(Image.open("CLIP.png")).unsqueeze(0).to(device)
text = clip.tokenize(["a diagram", "a dog", "a cat"]).to(device)

with torch.no_grad():
    logits_per_image, logits_per_text = model(image, text)
    probs = logits_per_image.softmax(dim=-1).cpu().numpy()

print("Label probs:", probs)
